transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

A lingering smell after a clean usually means it's coming from somewhere you can't easily see. The type of smell is the biggest clue, so here's a breakdown:

## If it's a rotten, musty or mouldy smell

These are the usual hidden culprits:

• Drip tray: Most fridge freezers have a tray at the back or underneath, near the compressor, where defrost water collects. It can get stagnant and mouldy. Pull the appliance out and check it (sometimes you need to remove a kick plate at the bottom front).
• Drain hole: There's usually a small hole at the back wall inside the fridge. If it's blocked with food debris, water pools and smells. Clear it with a cotton bud or pipe cleaner, then flush with warm water and a little bicarbonate of soda. Many fridges come with a little drain-cleaning tool.
• Door seals: Gunk and mould build up in the folds of the rubber gasket. Clean them with warm soapy water or diluted white vinegar and an old toothbrush.
• Behind drawers and shelves: Spills can seep underneath crisper drawers or into gaps.
• The freezer: If there's been a brief power cut or the door was left ajar, something may have thawed and refrozen. Check for anything that looks off.

To absorb leftover odour: leave an open tub of bicarbonate of soda, coffee grounds, or activated charcoal inside for a few days.

## If it's a burning, hot or electrical smell

This is more serious. It could be the compressor, fan motor, or wiring overheating.

• Unplug it and get it checked by an engineer.
• Also check that the area behind it isn't clogged with dust, as dusty condenser coils can overheat. Vacuuming them is worthwhile anyway.

## If it's a chemical, sweet or ammonia-like smell

This could be a refrigerant leak, especially if the fridge also isn't cooling properly. Ventilate the room and call an engineer. Don't try to fix this yourself.

## Other quick checks

• Is it still cooling properly? The fridge should be around 3–5°C and the freezer around -18°C. If it's warmer, food may be spoiling faster, pointing to a fault.
• Is it definitely the fridge? Smells can come from behind or under it: a dead mouse, a dropped bit of food, or a nearby sink trap or bin.

What does the smell actually resemble? Let me know and I can help narrow it down further.

It smells like hot plastic, a bit electrical, not like rotten food. It seems stronger round the back and side of the fridge than inside it, and the plug feels a little warm. I also hear a buzzing from the back now and then.

This needs treating as a possible fire risk. A hot plastic smell, a warm plug and buzzing together suggest something is overheating electrically, either in the plug, socket or wiring, or in a component at the back like the compressor relay or fan.

## Do this now

1. Switch off at the wall and unplug it. If the plug or socket is too hot to touch comfortably, or you see scorching, switch off at the socket (or the fuse box/consumer unit if needed) first, then unplug.
2. Don't plug it back in to "see if it's okay", and don't move it to another socket yet.
3. Check the plug and socket once unplugged:
• Any brown or black scorch marks, melted or discoloured plastic, or a burning smell from the socket itself?
• Are the plug pins discoloured?
4. If you see smoke, sparks or flames, get out and call 999. Don't use water on an electrical fire.

## What it could be

• Plug, fuse or socket fault: A loose connection or worn socket creates resistance and heat. This is common and often the source of a warm plug. If the socket shows damage, stop using it and get an electrician to look at it, as it's a fire risk for anything plugged into it.
• Fridge fault: A failing compressor start relay, fan motor or wiring at the back can buzz, overheat and give off that smell. This needs an appliance engineer.
• Extension lead or adaptor: If the fridge is plugged into one, that could be the cause. Fridge freezers should go directly into a wall socket.

## Getting it fixed

• If the socket looks damaged: call an electrician.
• If the socket looks fine: call an appliance repair engineer, or the manufacturer if it's under warranty. Have the model number ready (usually on a sticker inside the fridge).
• It's also worth checking whether your model has a product recall. Manufacturers and the UK government's product safety site list these.

## Your food

Keep the doors shut. The fridge should keep food cold for about 4 hours, and a full freezer for about 48 hours (24 if half-full). If it'll be longer, move essentials to a cool box with ice packs, or to a neighbour's fridge.

It's a hassle, but you were right to flag it. These symptoms shouldn't be ignored.
Ok, I'll unplug it now. The socket looks fine to me, no marks that I can see, and there's no smoke. The plug just felt a bit warm. Should I get an engineer in then?

Yes, get an appliance repair engineer. With the hot plastic smell from the back, the buzzing and a warm plug, the fault is most likely in the fridge itself (often the compressor start relay, fan motor or wiring). Leave it unplugged until it's been checked, as these faults can get worse and become a fire risk.

## Before you call

• Find the model and serial number. It's usually on a sticker inside the fridge compartment, sometimes on the back.
• Check the warranty. If it's under warranty, or you have appliance cover or home insurance that includes it, go through them first.
• Check for recalls. Search the model number on the manufacturer's site or the UK government's product recall list. If it's recalled, the repair or replacement should be free.
• Tell the engineer what you've noticed: hot plastic or electrical smell strongest at the back and side, buzzing, warm plug. It helps them diagnose it quickly.

## Worth knowing

• A plug can still have a hidden fault even if the socket looks fine, such as a loose wire or a poor connection on the fuse. Ask the engineer to check the plug and lead too.
• If the engineer finds nothing wrong with the fridge or plug, have an electrician check that socket before you use it for anything else, since faults behind the faceplate aren't always visible.
• If the fridge is old, ask whether repair is worth it. A new compressor can cost nearly as much as a new fridge freezer.

## Your food in the meantime

• Keep the doors shut as much as possible.
• The fridge will keep food safely cold for about 4 hours. A full freezer lasts about 48 hours, or about 24 hours if half full.
• If it's going to be longer, move the most important items (meat, fish, dairy, leftovers) to a cool box with ice packs, a neighbour's fridge, or eat them soon.
• Bin anything perishable that has been above 8°C for more than about 4 hours. If frozen food still has ice crystals, it's generally fine to refreeze.
